# Evidence tables

Certainty reflects the strength and consistency of the underlying evidence
(GRADE-style judgement), not the size of the effect. `Status` separates
established findings from emerging or unsupported ones.

| Does creatine plus resistance training increase upper-body maximal strength? | Bench or chest press 1RM | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 RCTs; 23 RCTs; 509 participants | +4.43 kg (95% CI 3.12 to 5.75) | Moderate | Established | R09 |
| Does creatine plus resistance training increase lower-body maximal strength? | Leg press 1RM | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 RCTs | +11.35 kg | Moderate | Established | R09 |
| Does creatine plus training improve squat strength? | Squat 1RM | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 69 studies; 69 studies; 1,937 participants | +5.64 kg | Moderate | Established | R10 |
| Does creatine improve vertical jump? | Countermovement or vertical jump height | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 69 studies; 69 studies; 1,937 participants | +1.48 cm | Moderate | Established | R10 |
| Does creatine increase anaerobic peak power? | Wingate peak power | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies; 12 studies; 21 intervention arms | +47.81 W (95% CI 15.55 to 80.06) | Moderate | Established | R10 |
| Does short-term creatine improve repeated-sprint performance? | Mean and peak power across repeated sprints | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 RCTs; 14 studies | Mean power SMD 0.61; peak power SMD 0.41 (not significant) | Low | Mixed | R34 |
| What is the typical acute ergogenic effect? | Maximal power and strength; sprint work | Narrative synthesis of controlled trials; Multiple trials | 5-15% for maximal power and strength; 1-5% for single-sprint; 5-15% for repeated-sprint work | Moderate | Established | R60 |
| Does creatine improve endurance performance? | Time trial, VO2max, aerobic capacity | Systematic review and umbrella review; Multiple trials | No clear aerobic benefit; possible benefit for surges and finishing sprints | Low | Mixed | R33, R16 |
| Does creatine plus resistance training improve strength in older adults? | Upper-body strength | Systematic review and meta-analysis; n=693 | SMD 0.24 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.43) | Moderate | Established | R14 |

## Muscle mass and body composition

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Pooled result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does creatine plus resistance training increase lean body mass? | Lean body mass | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies | +1.14 kg (95% CI 0.69 to 1.59) | Moderate | Established | R12 |
| Is the lean-mass effect present across ages? | Lean body mass | Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs; Multiple RCTs | +1.10 kg with resistance training regardless of age; +0.03 kg without exercise (95% CI 0.56 to 1.65 with training; -0.65 to 0.70 without) | Moderate | Established | R11 |
| Does creatine augment lean tissue in older adults? | Lean tissue mass | Systematic review and meta-analysis; n=746 | +1.18 kg (95% CI 0.70 to 1.67) | Moderate | Established | R14, R13 |
| Does creatine benefit postmenopausal women? | Lean mass and leg press strength | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 RCTs; 7 RCTs; n=608 | Lean mass +0.37 kg; leg press +7.5 kg (Lean mass 95% CI 0.05 to 0.69; leg press 2.2 to 12.8) | Low | Established | R17 |
| Do men and women respond differently in lean mass? | Lean body mass | Systematic review and meta-analysis; Multiple RCTs | Men +1.46 kg; women +0.29 kg (not significant) (Men 0.47 to 2.46; women -0.43 to 1.01) | Low | Mixed | R11 |
| Does creatine reduce fat mass? | Fat mass and body fat percentage | Systematic review and meta-analysis; 12 studies | Fat mass -0.73 kg; body fat -0.88 percentage points (Fat mass 95% CI -1.34 to -0.11) | Low | Emerging | R12 |
| Is a higher creatine dose better for lean mass? | Lean body mass | Systematic review and meta-analysis; 12 studies | About 7 g/day or 0.3 g/kg/day produced about 1 kg more lean mass than training alone | Low | Emerging | R12 |

## Cognition and brain health

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Pooled result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does creatine improve memory in healthy people? | Memory performance | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 8 RCTs | SMD 0.29 (95% CI 0.04 to 0.53) | Low | Emerging | R23 |
| Is the memory effect larger in older adults? | Memory performance | Subgroup meta-analysis; Subgroup of the 8 RCTs | SMD 0.88 (95% CI 0.22 to 1.55) | Low | Emerging | R23 |
| Does creatine improve cognition in healthy young adults? | Reasoning and working memory | Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover; n=123 | Small beneficial Bayesian signal; backward digit span p=0.064; reasoning task p=0.327 | Low | Mixed | R25 |
| Does creatine protect cognition during sleep loss? | Attention, reaction time, executive function | Systematic review and small RCTs; 5 publications from 4 trial cohorts, plus later pilot | Some benefit on selected executive and memory tasks; a 2026 pilot found no effect | Very low | Mixed | R30, R64 |
| Does creatine reduce depressive symptoms? | Depression rating scales | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 trials; 11 trials; n=1,093 | SMD -0.34, equivalent to about 2.2 points on HAM-D (95% CI -0.68 to 0.00) | Very low | Emerging | R26 |
| Does creatine improve outcomes after traumatic brain injury? | Post-concussion symptoms, recovery | Small trials and government review; Several small studies | Possible faster improvement in some trials; no large confirmatory RCT | Very low | Emerging | R27, R59 |
| Does creatine slow Parkinson's disease? | UPDRS and functional scales | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 RCTs; 5 RCTs; n=1,339 | No significant benefit on total, mental, ADL or motor UPDRS | Moderate | Unsupported | R28 |
| Is creatine associated with better cognition in older adults? | Memory and attention | Systematic review of 6 studies; 6 studies; n=1,542 | 5 of 6 studies reported a positive association | Very low | Emerging | R24, R29 |

## Safety and risk

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Pooled result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How common are adverse events overall? | Any adverse event | Pooled analysis of clinical trials and adverse-event reports; 685 studies up to 14 years | 13.7% vs 13.2% of studies reported side effects; not significant (p=0.776) | High | Established | R35 |
| Does creatine cause gastrointestinal upset? | GI adverse events | Pooled analysis; 685 studies | 5.51% vs 4.05% of participants; not significant (p=0.820) | Moderate | Established | R35 |
| Does creatine cause muscle cramps? | Cramping or muscle pain | Pooled analysis; 685 studies | 0.52% vs 0.07% of participants; not significant (p=0.085) | Moderate | Established | R35 |
| Does creatine raise serum creatinine? | Serum creatinine | Systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 studies; 26 studies; n=1,036 | +0.14 mg/dL (95% CI 0.05 to 0.22) | High | Established | R38 |
| Does creatine reduce creatinine-based eGFR? | eGFR calculated from creatinine | Systematic review and meta-analysis; 26 studies | -10.75 mL/min/1.73 m2 (95% CI -17.48 to -4.02) | High | Established | R38 |
| Does creatine change measured GFR? | GFR by chromium-51 EDTA | Systematic review and meta-analysis; Subset of studies | +5.89 mL/min/1.73 m2, not significant (95% CI -0.30 to 12.08) | Moderate | Established | R38 |
| Does creatine affect liver markers? | Liver enzymes and liver disease prevalence | Observational NHANES analysis and safety review; Large national sample | No association with liver disease manifestations; no adverse liver signal in trials | Moderate | Established | R63, R40 |
| Does creatine cause hair loss? | DHT, hair density, follicle counts | 12-week RCT and earlier crossover trial; 38 completers in the RCT; 20 in the earlier trial | No difference in DHT or any hair outcome vs placebo (p>0.05) | Moderate | Unsupported | R43, R44 |
| Does creatine impair hydration or thermoregulation? | Total body water, sweat rate, core temperature | Systematic review with meta-analyses and controlled trials; 10 studies in the meta-analysis | No impairment; intracellular water may increase | High | Established | R41, R40, R62 |
| How much weight does creatine add? | Body mass | Meta-analysis and controlled trials; Multiple studies | About 0.8-1.5 kg with loading, mostly intracellular water | High | Established | R34, R40 |
| Is creatine safe in chronic kidney disease? | Renal function, proteinuria | Narrative reviews and small trials; Limited | Insufficient evidence; theoretical risk and diagnostic confusion | Very low | Unsupported | R36, R40 |
| Are there clinically important drug interactions? | Adverse outcomes with prescription drugs | Evidence-mapping review of interaction databases; No controlled human interaction studies | No moderate or high severity interactions established; signals are minor and theoretical | Very low | Emerging | R42 |
| Does creatine increase cancer risk? | Cancer incidence | Narrative review of human and animal data; No human evidence of increased risk | No increased risk demonstrated | Low | Unsupported | R40 |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Do vegetarians and vegans respond more to creatine? | Muscle creatine stores | Systematic review of 9 studies | Vegetarians have lower baseline stores and larger increases with supplementation | Moderate | Established | R31 |

| Does creatine affect fluid balance across the menstrual cycle? | Total body water and body mass | Randomised controlled trial; n=20 | Increased total body water in the luteal phase without a body-mass difference | Low | Emerging | R20 |
| Is creatine safe and effective in adolescents? | Performance and safety | Narrative review; Limited trials | Short-term use appears safe in supervised settings; long-term data are lacking | Low | Emerging | R02 |

## Dosing, timing, and protocols

| Question | Outcome | Evidence base | Pooled result | Certainty | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What is a creatine loading protocol? | Muscle creatine saturation | Position stand and classic physiology; Multiple trials | 20-25 g/day (0.3 g/kg/day) in 4-5 divided doses for 5-7 days | High | Established | R01 |
| What maintenance dose is needed? | Muscle creatine maintenance | Position stand; Multiple trials | 3-5 g/day; larger athletes may need 5-10 g/day | High | Established | R01 |
| Can you skip the loading phase? | Muscle creatine saturation | Classic comparison trial summarised in position stand; Multiple trials | 3 g/day for 28 days produces similar saturation to loading | Moderate | Established | R01 |
| Does timing around exercise matter? | Strength and lean mass | Narrative reviews and an 8-week RCT; Multiple studies | Pre-, post-, and non-training-day dosing produce similar adaptations | Moderate | Established | R55, R56, R57, R58 |
| Does daily consistency matter? | Muscle creatine maintenance | Position stand and physiology; Multiple trials | Daily intake is required to maintain saturated stores; missed days gradually deplete them | High | Established | R01 |

| Are creatine products contaminated with heavy metals? | Lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury | Laboratory surveys; 33 products in one survey; 12 products in a 2025 testing programme | Most products low; occasional lead exceedance in gummies; powders performed well | Moderate | Established | R45, R46 |

| How stable is creatine in powder and in solution? | Creatine degradation to creatinine | Laboratory studies; Multiple | Dry powder is stable for years; in solution, degradation accelerates with heat and acidity | High | Established | R02, R53, R54 |
